# pamflow

**End-to-end Passive Acoustic Monitoring workflow**

`pamflow` takes you from raw field recordings to ecological useful
information — with a single config file and a handful of function calls.

`Workflow A (Species Detection & Occupancy)`: Run BirdNET, clean & merge
detections, perform stratified validation with Shiny, build daily site
occupancy matrices, and compile executive reports.

`Workflow B (Soundscape Analysis)`: Compute core acoustic indices (ACI,
ADI, AEve, Bio, H, M, NDSI) following Bradfer-Lawrence et al. (2019)
with 500 Hz low-stop filtering, 1-minute memory-safe sub-chunking,
24-hour diel profiles, and automated HTML diagnostic reports.

## Features

- **Raven Compass-style Standardization & Triage** for raw
  multi-recorder workflow (SongMeter, AudioMoth, SwiftOne)
- **Scan & QC** thousands of WAV files automatically
- **Batch BirdNET detection** with parallel workers and resume support
  (runs the Python `birdnet` package; no birdnetR needed)
- **Clean & merge** overlapping detections into events
- **Interactive validation** via Shiny app with precision metrics
- **Occupancy detection histories** (1/0 matrices per site per species;
  occasion length set in the config)
- **Activity, richness and diversity** from the detections and the
  recording effort: species thresholds from validation, activity
  patterns by hour or season, Hill numbers, species accumulation
- **Input for occupancy and abundance models** (`unmarked`, `ubms`,
  `spOccupancy`): count histories for one or many species and seasons,
  with covariates and checks. pamflow prepares the data; it does not fit
  the models
- **Standalone BirdNET training tool** (separate from the workflow):
  train your own classifier from R or in a point-and-click app, with
  per-class test results
- **Ecoacoustic Soundscape Indices** Dynamic computation of ACI, ADI,
  AEve, Bio, H, M, and NDSI.
- **Soundscape Visualizations & HTML Reports** 24-hour diel profiles,
  Day vs. Night comparisons, site covariate tables, and standalone HTML
  reports.

## Prerequisites

| Software | Version | Notes                                                    |
|----------|---------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| R        | ≥ 4.3   | 64-bit                                                   |
| uv       | latest  | Creates pamflow’s private Python environment for BirdNET |
| FFmpeg   | any     | Required for audio clipping                              |

On Windows install uv with `winget install --id astral-sh.uv` (other
systems: see <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/>). pamflow downloads the Python
version it needs, so no system Python is required.

Verify in R after installing pamflow:

``` r

R.version.string           # ≥ 4.3
system("ffmpeg -version")  # prints version
pamflow::pam_birdnet_doctor()
```

## Installation

``` r

# Install devtools if needed
install.packages("devtools")

# Install pamflow
devtools::install_github("pradeeshwarrj/pamflow")

# Create the Python environment BirdNET runs in (once; downloads TensorFlow, a few minutes)
pamflow::pam_birdnet_setup("inference")
# Optional, only for the standalone model-training tool (see "Training a custom BirdNET classifier"):
pamflow::pam_birdnet_setup("training")
```

## Try it without any data

[`pam_example_project()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_example_project.md)
builds a tiny synthetic project in a temporary folder: six short
recordings, a deployment sheet, a config and a small detections file.
You can see how the stages work before using your own recordings. It
needs no FFmpeg, Python or internet connection.

``` r

library(pamflow)

ex <- pam_example_project()             # created in a temporary folder
res <- pam_scan_audio(ex$cfg)           # Stage 1: scan the recordings
res$summary$overall                     # files, grids, hours, QC results

out <- pam_process_detections(ex$cfg)   # Stage 4: clean the example detections
out$steps                               # what each cleaning rule removed

occ <- pam_build_occupancy(ex$cfg)      # Stage 6: detection histories
occ$histories[[1]]

act <- pam_activity(ex$cfg)             # activity by hour of the day
rich <- pam_richness(ex$cfg)            # richness and diversity per site
rich$sites
```

Open `ex$root` in your file browser to see what each stage wrote. Every
help page has an example built on this project, for instance
[`?pam_validation_draw`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_draw.md)
or `example("pam_scan_audio")`. To keep the sandbox, give it a folder:
`pam_example_project("C:/pamflow_sandbox")`.

## Quick Start

### 1. Set up your project folder

``` R
MyProject/
├── data/
│   └── raw/                # Original recorder dumps (untouched)
│       ├── SongMeter/
│       ├── AudioMoth/
│       └── SwiftOne/
├── metadata/
│   └── deployments.csv     # one row per deployment
├── models/
│   └── custom_classifier/  # your .tflite model and _Labels.txt
└── config/
    └── config.yml          # your settings
```

pamflow creates the other folders (`data/standardized/`,
`data/detections/`, `data/occupancy/`, `logs/`, `reports/` …) as the
stages run.

### 2. Create `metadata/deployments.csv`

One row per deployment. Columns are read by position, so keep this order
(dates as `dd-mm-yyyy`, times as `hh:mm`; give the grid as a number, for
example `59` for `G0059`):

``` csv
deployment_id,recorder,grid,habitat,deployer,latitude,longitude,deploy_date,deploy_time,retrieve_date,retrieve_time
13,SW010,59,Forest,Asha,7.01,93.82,05-04-2026,18:30,08-04-2026,16:00
7,SW012,110,Plantation,Ravi,7.05,93.85,01-04-2026,06:00,10-04-2026,18:00
```

### 3. Create `config/config.yml`

You only need to set what differs from the defaults; every setting you
leave out falls back to the template that ships with pamflow.

``` yaml
paths:
  project_root: "E:/MyProject"          # all other paths are relative to this folder

filenames:
  pattern: "^(?<grid>G\\d{4})_(?<date>\\d{8})_(?<time>\\d{6})(_chunk\\d+)?\\.(flac|wav)$"
  timezone: "Asia/Kolkata"

birdnet:
  run_id: "run01"
  model_dir: "models/custom_classifier"   # folder with your .tflite and _Labels.txt
  classifier_name: "CustomClassifier"     # files: <name>.tflite and <name>_Labels.txt
  min_confidence: 0.3
  workers: null                           # null = half of the physical cores

occupancy:
  run_id: "run01"
  occasion_length_days: 1
```

To see every setting, copy the full template and edit it:

``` r

file.copy(system.file("extdata", "config_template.yml", package = "pamflow"),
          "config/config.yml")
```

### 4. Run the pipeline

Stage 00: Standardization & Data Triage (Raven Compass)

Raw multi-recorder dumps are often messy (mixed formats, voice memos,
field notes, inconsistent filenames). Stage 00 standardizes them without
modifying original raw files.

### Interactive Shiny App

``` r

library(pamflow)
pam_standardization_app()
```

The GUI provides three tabs:

- **Inspect** — Preview files, extract metadata, test filename regex

- **Convert** — Batch convert and organize into standardized folders

- **Log** — Live processing log

The validation
([`pam_validate()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validate.md))
and annotation
([`pam_annotate()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_annotate.md))
apps share this look, with a light and dark mode.

### Headless Standardization R

``` r

library(pamflow)
cfg <- pam_config_read("E:/MyProject/config/config.yml")

pam_standardize(cfg)     # raw -> data/standardized, memos and non-audio -> data/isolated
```

#### What Stage 00 does:

- Extracts grid IDs and timestamps from SongMeter, AudioMoth, and
  SwiftOne filenames

- Isolates voice memos (\< 60 s), text logs, and unreadable files into
  data/isolated/

- Converts and renames audio into a uniform structure under
  data/standardized/G####/

- Leaves all original raw files untouched

## Workflow A: Detection & Occupancy Pipeline

``` r

library(pamflow)
cfg <- pam_config_read("E:/MyProject/config/config.yml")

# Stage 00: Standardize raw recorder dumps (if not done via Shiny app)
pam_standardize(cfg)

# Stage 1: Scan audio and check deployments
pam_scan_audio(cfg)

# Stage 2 (optional): high-pass filter the QC-passed files
# pam_filter_audio(cfg)

# Stage 3: Run BirdNET detection (parallel, resumable)
pam_detect(cfg)

# Stage 4: Clean, filter, and merge detections
pam_process_detections(cfg)

# Stage 5: Validate a sample of detections
pam_validation_draw(cfg)
pam_validation_export(cfg)
pam_validation_app(cfg)          # opens Shiny app in browser

# After closing the app:
val  <- pam_validation_import(cfg)
pool <- pam_validation_pool(cfg)
pam_validation_metrics(val, pool, bands = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9))

# Stage 5b (optional): ground-truth segments to estimate recall
# pam_recall_draw(cfg); pam_recall_export(cfg)

# Stage 6: Build occupancy detection histories
pam_build_occupancy(cfg)

# Stage 7: Input for occupancy and abundance models (you fit them yourself)
hist <- pam_count_history(cfg, species = "Gracula religiosa")
x <- pam_model_input(hist, binary = TRUE)   # y, siteCovs, obsCovs

# Stage 8: Generate species detection reports
pam_report(cfg)
```

## Workflow B: Soundscape Analysis Pipeline

``` r

library(pamflow)
cfg <- pam_config_read("E:/MyProject/config/config.yml")

# Stage 00: Standardize raw recorder dumps
pam_standardize(cfg)

# Stage 1: Scan audio and check deployments
pam_scan_audio(cfg)

# Stage 2b: Calculate soundscape indices (ACI, Bio, NDSI, etc.)
sc_results <- pam_soundscape_run(cfg)

# Stage 2c: Generate 24-hour diel plots, Day/Night comparisons & HTML Report
vis_results <- pam_soundscape_run_vis(cfg)
```

## Beyond occupancy: activity, richness and model input

The cleaned detections can answer more than occupancy questions. These
functions use the recording effort, so sites and periods recorded for
different lengths of time can be compared. pamflow prepares the input
for occupancy and abundance models but does not fit them: use
`unmarked`, `ubms`, `spOccupancy` or any other package.

``` r

# One confidence threshold per species, from the Stage 5 validation
thr <- pam_species_thresholds(cfg, write = TRUE)

# Activity: detections per recorded hour, by hour of day, day, week or month
act <- pam_activity(cfg, by = "hour")
pam_plot_activity(act)

# Richness, Hill numbers, species accumulation and the Chao2 estimate
rich <- pam_richness(cfg)
rich$sites
pam_plot_richness(rich)

# Input for occupancy and abundance models (one species, or many, and seasons)
hist <- pam_count_history(cfg, species = "Gracula religiosa")
x <- pam_model_input(hist, binary = TRUE)    # y, siteCovs, obsCovs
pam_check_model_input(x)
umf <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccu(y = x$y, siteCovs = x$siteCovs, obsCovs = x$obsCovs)
```

Occasions follow `occupancy.occasion_length_days` in the config. See the
guide
([`vignette("pamflow-guide")`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/articles/pamflow-guide.md))
for several species, several seasons and the details of each function.

## Pipeline Stages

| Workflow | Stage | Function | What it does |
|----|----|----|----|
| Both | 00 | [`pam_standardize()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_standardize.md) / [`pam_standardization_app()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_standardization_app.md) | Raven Compass-style triage: metadata extraction, memo isolation (\<60s), non-audio log separation, FLAC/WAV standardization |
| Both | 1 | [`pam_scan_audio()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_scan_audio.md) | Inventories audio files, matches to deployments, flags QC issues |
| Both | 2 | [`pam_filter_audio()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_filter_audio.md) | High-pass filter on the QC checked files; can be customized |
| B | 2b | [`pam_soundscape_run()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_run.md) | Computes soundscape indices per 10-min window with 500Hz high-pass filter |
| B | 2c | [`pam_soundscape_run_vis()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_run_vis.md) | Plots 24-hour diel profiles, Day/Night comparisons, and generates HTML report |
| A | 3 | [`pam_detect()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_detect.md) | Runs BirdNET on all files in parallel batches; resumable |
| A | 4 | [`pam_process_detections()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_process_detections.md) | Filters by confidence, deployment window, species; merges overlapping windows |
| A | 5 | [`pam_validation_draw()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_draw.md) | Draws a stratified random sample for manual review |
| A | 5 | [`pam_validation_export()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_export.md) | Cuts short WAV clips around each sampled detection |
| A | 5 | `pam_validation_app()` | Shiny app to listen and confirm/reject species |
| A | 5 | [`pam_validation_metrics()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_metrics.md) | Computes precision by species and confidence band |
| A | 5b | [`pam_recall_draw()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_draw.md) / [`pam_recall_export()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_export.md) / [`pam_recall_metrics()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_metrics.md) | Optional ground-truth segments to estimate recall |
| A | 6 | [`pam_build_occupancy()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_build_occupancy.md) | Builds detection matrices (occasion length from the config), effort, and site covariates |
| A | 7 | [`pam_count_history()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_count_history.md) / [`pam_count_histories()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_count_histories.md) | Counts of one or many species by site and occasion, with effort and covariates |
| A | 7 | [`pam_model_input()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_model_input.md) / [`pam_define_seasons()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_define_seasons.md) / [`pam_check_model_input()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_check_model_input.md) | Input for `unmarked`, `ubms` or `spOccupancy`, for one or many species and seasons, checked before fitting |
| A | Eco | [`pam_species_thresholds()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_species_thresholds.md) | One confidence threshold per species from the validation |
| A | Eco | [`pam_activity()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_activity.md) / [`pam_richness()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_richness.md) | Activity patterns and species richness and diversity from the detections |
| A | 8 | [`pam_report()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_report.md) | Generates HTML, PDF and Excel reports, including richness and activity |

> **Note:** All stage functions take `cfg` as their primary argument.
> The run_id is read from the config file. Stage 00 can also be run
> interactively via
> [`pam_standardization_app()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_standardization_app.md).

## Training a custom BirdNET classifier (standalone tool)

Training your own classifier is **separate from the workflow**: it is
not a pipeline stage, no stage function calls it, and the workflow runs
without it. Use it when you need a `.tflite` model to give to Stage 3.

``` r

# Once: the training environment (downloads BirdNET-Analyzer and TensorFlow)
pamflow::pam_birdnet_setup("training")

# Point-and-click app, laid out like the BirdNET-Analyzer GUI training tab
pamflow::pam_train_app()

# Or from code
pamflow::pam_birdnet_train_prepare("E:/clips")            # check the training folder
res <- pamflow::pam_birdnet_train("E:/clips", "E:/models/MyModel",
                                  test_data = "E:/clips_test")
res$evaluation$classes                                     # precision, recall, F1, AUPRC, AUROC per class
```

It runs BirdNET-Analyzer’s own `birdnet-train` (version 2.4.0), so
results match the Analyzer GUI, and it works on Windows without WSL or a
GPU. The app shows live progress and learning curves, per-class test
results, earlier runs, a light and dark theme, and the `birdnet:` config
lines for the new model. To use the model, set `birdnet$model_dir` and
`birdnet$classifier_name` in your config.

## Outputs

``` R
MyProject/
├── data/
│   ├── raw/                         # Original recorder dumps (never modified)
│   ├── standardized/                # Standardized audio (from Stage 00)
│   │   ├── G0059/
│   │   └── G0110/
│   ├── isolated/                    # Memos, logs, corrupt files (from Stage 00)
│   ├── filtered/                    # Only if you run the optional filter (Stage 2)
│   ├── soundscape/run01/
│   │   ├── soundscape_raw.csv
│   │   ├── soundscape_hourly.csv
│   │   ├── soundscape_diel_summary.csv
│   │   ├── soundscape_site_covariates.csv
│   │   ├── plots/
│   │   │   ├── diel_hourly_aci.png
│   │   │   └── diel_phase_aci.png
│   │   └── reports/
│   │       └── Soundscape_Report_run01.html
│   ├── detections/run01/
│   │   ├── batches/
│   │   ├── processed/
│   │   └── validation/              # Sampled events, clips and your verdicts (Stage 5)
│   ├── validation/ground_truth/     # Recall segments (Stage 5b)
│   └── occupancy/run01/
│       ├── detection_matrices/
│       ├── effort.csv
│       ├── site_covariates.csv
│       └── occupancy_summary.csv
├── metadata/
│   ├── audio_headers.csv
│   └── audio_master.csv             # Every recording with deployment match and QC flags
├── outputs/
│   ├── deployment_issues.csv
│   └── audio_summary_per_grid.csv
├── reports/
└── logs/
```

## Configuration Reference

The most-used settings and their defaults (the full list is in the
template, see step 3 above).

| Section | Key | Default | Description |
|----|----|----|----|
| `filenames` | `timezone` | `"Asia/Kolkata"` | Timezone for filename date-times and deployment dates |
| `standardization` | `min_duration_s` | 60 | Files shorter than this are isolated as memos |
| `standardization` | `target_format` | `"flac"` | Output audio format (`flac` or `wav`) |
| `birdnet` | `run_id` | `"run01"` | Name of this detection run |
| `birdnet` | `input` | `"standardized"` | Audio to scan: `"standardized"` or `"filtered"` |
| `birdnet` | `model_dir` | `"models/custom_classifier"` | Folder with your `.tflite` model and `_Labels.txt` |
| `birdnet` | `classifier_name` | `"CustomClassifier"` | Model file name without `.tflite` |
| `birdnet` | `workers` | `null` | Worker processes; `null` = half of the physical cores |
| `birdnet` | `min_confidence` | 0.3 | Minimum BirdNET score to keep |
| `birdnet` | `chunk_size` | 100 | Files per batch; progress is saved after each batch |
| `processing` | `min_confidence` | 0.5 | Minimum confidence kept after processing |
| `processing` | `merge_gap_s` | 3 | Gap (seconds) for merging overlapping detections |
| `processing` | `drop_outside_deployment` | `true` | Remove detections outside deployment windows |
| `processing` | `species_thresholds_file` | `null` | CSV with `scientific_name` and `threshold`; see [`pam_species_thresholds()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_species_thresholds.md) |
| `occupancy` | `occasion_length_days` | 1 | Days per occasion; also the default time bin of the Stage 7 and ecological functions |
| `occupancy` | `min_effort_hours` | 2 | Minimum recording hours in an occasion for it to count as surveyed |
| `occupancy` | `min_detections` | 10 | Minimum total detections to include a species |

## Resumability

If
[`pam_detect()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_detect.md)
is interrupted (power loss, crash, etc.), simply run it again. It checks
for completed batches and picks up where it left off.

## Citing BirdNET and pamflow

pamflow runs BirdNET but does not include it. If you use pamflow with
BirdNET, please cite the BirdNET paper:

> Kahl, S., Wood, C. M., Eibl, M. and Klinck, H. (2021). BirdNET: A deep
> learning solution for avian diversity monitoring. *Ecological
> Informatics*, 61, 101236.
> <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecoinf.2021.101236>

The BirdNET models and the BirdNET-Analyzer are licensed by their
authors (research and educational use is non-commercial and free; check
each model’s license before other uses). To cite pamflow itself, run
`citation("pamflow")`.

  : Read and validate a pamflow configuration file

  : Validate a pamflow configuration
- [`pam_load_config()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_load_config.md)
  : Alias for pam_config_read

A small synthetic project (audio, deployment sheet, config) used by the
examples in this reference.

- [`pam_example_project()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_example_project.md)
  : Create a small example project to try pamflow on

- [`utils_audio`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/utils_audio.md)
  : Audio I/O Utilities (WAV + FLAC)
- [`pam_audio_exts()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_audio_exts.md)
  : Supported Audio File Extensions
- [`pam_audio_pattern()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_audio_pattern.md)
  : Regex Pattern Matching Supported Audio Files
- [`pam_is_flac()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_is_flac.md)
  : Check if a File is a FLAC File
- [`pam_read_audio()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_read_audio.md)
  : Read Audio File as a tuneR Wave Object (WAV or FLAC)
- [`pam_cut_audio()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_cut_audio.md)
  : Cut Audio Clip Preserving Source Format

## Stage 0 — Standardization & Triage

- [`pam_standardize()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_standardize.md)
  : Standardize Raw PAM Audio Files (Stage 00 Engine)
- [`pam_standardization_app()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_standardization_app.md)
  : Launch PAM Standardization & Data Triage Shiny App

  : Inspect Raw Audio Directory

  : Parse Datetime from Audio Filename or Metadata
- [`pam_extract_grid()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_extract_grid.md)
  : Extract Grid, Recorder, or Site Identifier from Filename

## Stage 1 — Scan & QC

- [`pam_scan_audio()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_scan_audio.md)
  : Stage 1: scan standardized audio and build the master metadata table
- [`pam_audio_info()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_audio_info.md)
  [`pam_audio_info_dt()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_audio_info.md)
  : Read Audio File Metadata (WAV or FLAC)
- [`pam_audio_summary()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_audio_summary.md)
  : Summarize the audio master table
- [`pam_list_audio()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_list_audio.md)
  : List Audio Files in a Directory (WAV + FLAC)
- [`pam_parse_filenames()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_parse_filenames.md)
  : Parse grid and start time from recording filenames
- [`pam_read_deployments()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_read_deployments.md)
  : Read and clean the deployment sheet
- [`pam_match_deployments()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_match_deployments.md)
  : Attach recorder and coordinates by matching grid and time window
- [`pam_check_deployments()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_check_deployments.md)
  : List problems in the deployment table
- [`pam_add_qc()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_add_qc.md)
  : Add QC flags to a master audio table

## Stage 2 — Filter

- [`pam_filter_audio()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_filter_audio.md)
  : Stage 2: high-pass filter all QC-passed recordings
- [`pam_filter_one()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_filter_one.md)
  : Filter one audio file with FFmpeg (WAV or FLAC)
- [`pam_highpass_filter_string()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_highpass_filter_string.md)
  : Build the FFmpeg filter string for a Butterworth high-pass

## Stage 2b — Soundscape Indices

- [`soundscape`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/soundscape.md)
  : Stage 2b: Soundscape Analysis (Indices & Summaries)
- [`pam_soundscape_run()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_run.md)
  : Run Stage 2b Soundscape Analysis Pipeline
- [`pam_soundscape_one()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_one.md)
  : Compute Ecoacoustic Soundscape Indices for a Single Audio File
- [`pam_soundscape_batch()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_batch.md)
  : Batch Process Audio Files for Soundscape Indices
- [`pam_soundscape_summarise()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_summarise.md)
  : Summarize Soundscape Indices into Hourly, Diel, and Site Covariate
  Metrics
- [`to_scalar_num()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/to_scalar_num.md)
  : Safely Extract a Single Numeric Value from Soundecology/Seewave
  Returns

## Stage 2c — Soundscape Visualizations & Reports

- [`soundscape_vis`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/soundscape_vis.md)
  : Stage 2c: Soundscape Visualization & Diagnostics
- [`pam_soundscape_run_vis()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_run_vis.md)
  : Run Stage 2c Soundscape Visualization Pipeline
- [`pam_soundscape_plot_diel()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_plot_diel.md)
  : Plot 24-Hour Diel Curves for Acoustic Indices
- [`pam_soundscape_plot_phase()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_plot_phase.md)
  : Plot Day vs. Night Comparisons for Acoustic Indices
- [`pam_soundscape_report()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_soundscape_report.md)
  : Generate HTML Soundscape Diagnostic Report

## Stage 3 — Detect

- [`pam_detect()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_detect.md)
  : Stage 3: run the custom BirdNET classifier on all QC-passed
  recordings
- [`pam_assemble_detections()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_assemble_detections.md)
  : Assemble raw detection batches into one detections table
- [`pam_pending_batches()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_pending_batches.md)
  : Split pending work into batches, skipping completed items

## Stage 4 — Process

- [`pam_process_detections()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_process_detections.md)
  : Stage 4: clean the detections of a run
- [`pam_clean_detections()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_clean_detections.md)
  : Apply the cleaning rules to a detections table

## Stage 5 — Validate

- [`pam_validate()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validate.md)
  : Open the validation app
- [`pam_validation_draw()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_draw.md)
  : Draw a validation round and add it to the sample file
- [`pam_validation_export()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_export.md)
  : Export audio clips and spectrograms for the sampled events (WAV +
  FLAC)
- [`pam_validation_sample()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_sample.md)
  : Draw a validation sample from a pool of events
- [`pam_validation_import()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_import.md)
  : Join the reviewed verdicts to the sample table
- [`pam_validation_pool()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_pool.md)
  : Build the pool of candidate events for validation
- [`pam_validation_metrics()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_metrics.md)
  : Precision by species and confidence band, and by confidence
  threshold
- [`pam_validation_report()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_validation_report.md)
  : Validation report: precision tables written to disk
- [`pam_annotate()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_annotate.md)
  : Open the ground-truth annotation app

## Stage 5b — Recall

- [`pam_recall_draw()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_draw.md)
  : Draw a round of random segments for ground-truth annotation
- [`pam_recall_export()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_export.md)
  : Export audio and spectrograms for the ground-truth segments
- [`pam_recall_frame()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_frame.md)
  : All possible annotation segments of the recordings
- [`pam_recall_sample()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_sample.md)
  : Simple random sample of segments
- [`pam_recall_metrics()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_metrics.md)
  : Segment-level recall, precision and F1 against ground truth
- [`pam_recall_report()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_recall_report.md)
  : Recall report for a detection run

## Stage 6 — Occupancy

- [`pam_build_occupancy()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_build_occupancy.md)
  : Build occupancy detection histories for all qualifying species
- [`pam_site_id()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_site_id.md)
  : Build site identifiers from the audio master table
- [`pam_daily_effort()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_daily_effort.md)
  : Calculate daily recording effort per site
- [`pam_detection_matrix()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_detection_matrix.md)
  : Build a detection history matrix for one species
- [`pam_occasion_covariates()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_occasion_covariates.md)
  : Build occasion-level covariate table
- [`pam_site_covariates()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_site_covariates.md)
  : Build site-level covariate table

## Ecological products

Per-species thresholds and a site, time-bin and species table with
recording effort; activity patterns and richness.

- [`pam_species_thresholds()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_species_thresholds.md)
  : Choose a confidence threshold for each species from the validation
  results
- [`pam_detection_table()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_detection_table.md)
  : Table of detections and recording effort per site, time bin and
  species
- [`pam_activity()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_activity.md)
  : Activity patterns: detections per recorded hour
- [`pam_plot_activity()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_plot_activity.md)
  : Plot activity patterns
- [`pam_richness()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_richness.md)
  : Species richness and diversity per site and occasion
- [`pam_plot_richness()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_plot_richness.md)
  : Plot species richness

## Stage 7 — Input for occupancy and abundance models

Count histories per species and site, covariates, seasons, and input
ready for unmarked, ubms or spOccupancy. pamflow prepares the data; it
does not fit the models.

- [`pam_count_history()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_count_history.md)
  : Count history of one species: detections per site and occasion
- [`pam_count_histories()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_count_histories.md)
  : Count histories of many species at once
- [`pam_as_count_history()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_as_count_history.md)
  : Make a count history from your own counts
- [`pam_add_site_covariates()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_add_site_covariates.md)
  : Add site covariates to a count history
- [`pam_define_seasons()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_define_seasons.md)
  : Define seasons from the occasions of a history
- [`pam_model_input()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_model_input.md)
  : Prepare a count history as input for abundance and occupancy models
- [`pam_check_model_input()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_check_model_input.md)
  : Check model input before fitting

## Stage 8 — Reports

- [`pam_report()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_report.md)
  : Generate PAM workflow reports
- [`pam_report_data()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_report_data.md)
  : Gather report data from all completed stages
- [`pam_report_excel()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_report_excel.md)
  : Write summary tables to an Excel workbook

## Standalone tool — BirdNET model training (not a workflow stage)

Train your own BirdNET classifier from R or in a point-and-click app.
Nothing in the workflow calls these functions; the trained model is used
by pointing the `birdnet:` section of the config at it.

- [`pam_train_app()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_train_app.md)
  : Launch the BirdNET classifier training app

- [`pam_birdnet_train_prepare()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_train_prepare.md)
  : Check a training dataset before training

- [`pam_birdnet_train()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_train.md)
  : Train a custom BirdNET classifier from R

- [`pam_birdnet_train_repeat()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_train_repeat.md)
  : Train the same classifier several times and summarize the metrics

- [`pam_birdnet_train_metrics()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_train_metrics.md)
  :

  Read training metrics from a `birdnet-train` log

## BirdNET environment & benchmark

- [`pam_birdnet_setup()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_setup.md)
  : Create a private Python environment for BirdNET
- [`pam_birdnet_doctor()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_doctor.md)
  : Check the machine and Python environments needed for BirdNET
- [`pam_birdnet_cleanup()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_cleanup.md)
  : Stop BirdNET worker processes that were left behind
- [`pam_birdnet_benchmark()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_birdnet_benchmark.md)
  : Benchmark Stage 3 detection speed at several worker counts

## Utilities

- [`pam_audio_history()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_audio_history.md)
  : Follow audio files through the workflow
- [`pam_log()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_log.md)
  : Write a timestamped log line to a per-stage log file
- [`pam_run_stage()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_run_stage.md)
  : Run a workflow stage with logging and error isolation
- [`pam_checkpoint_read()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_checkpoint_read.md)
  : Read the set of already-processed item IDs
- [`pam_checkpoint_add()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_checkpoint_add.md)
  : Record items as completed
- [`pam_check_ffmpeg()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_check_ffmpeg.md)
  : Check that FFmpeg is installed and supports the filter chain
- [`pam_wilson_ci()`](https://pradeeshwarrj.github.io/pamflow/reference/pam_wilson_ci.md)
  : Wilson score confidence interval for a proportion
